cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader. Anyone with an infectious skin disease had to live alone outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46). Now God gives the law for the day that person is cleansed.

cards.question: On the day of cleansing, where does the priest go to examine the person with the skin disease?

cards.text: He's out there to check whether the skin disease has healed. A HOUSE CALL, friend, and I spent years in a junk drawer without anybody coming by to check on me!
If it has healed, the priest orders two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop. One bird is slaughtered over fresh water in a clay pot.

cards.question: The priest dips the live bird, the cedar wood, the yarn and the hyssop into the blood of the slaughtered bird. How many times does he sprinkle the one being cleansed?
After the sprinkling, the priest pronounces the person clean.
The priest still has the live bird that was dipped in the blood. What happens to it?

answers.text: It's released into the open field
It's offered up on the altar
It's given to the priest's family

cards.text: Next, the person washes his clothes, shaves off all his hair and bathes with water, and he's ceremonially clean. He can come back into the camp, but he's not all the way home yet.

cards.question: The person being cleansed is back in the camp. For seven days, where must he stay?

cards.text: That's getting locked out on the porch for a WEEK with your keys on the counter inside. On the seventh day, he shaves off all his hair again, eyebrows included, and with eyebrows like mine that's a full day's work.

cards.question: After that second shave, he washes his clothes and bathes himself with ___, and he will be clean.

cards.text: On the eighth day, he brings two unblemished male lambs, an unblemished ewe lamb a year old, fine flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, and a log of olive oil. That's a lot to carry, friend.

cards.question: The priest presents the person and all these offerings before the LORD. Where?

answers.text: At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting
Out in the open field by the camp
Beside the river outside the camp

cards.text: The priest waves one male lamb as a guilt offering, with the log of olive oil, before the LORD. Then he slaughters it in the sanctuary area.

cards.question: Where does the priest put some of the guilt offering's blood on the one being cleansed?

answers.text: His right earlobe and thumb and big toe
His forehead and both of his hands
His left ear and his left foot

cards.text: Then he sprinkles some of the oil seven times before the LORD and puts oil on those same spots, right on top of the blood. Me, I measure chocolate chips by squinting at the bowl and going, eh, close enough.

cards.question: Whatever oil is left in his palm, the priest puts on the head of the one being cleansed. What does the text say it's for?

answers.text: To make atonement for him before the LORD
To show he can serve as a priest
To heal what's left of his skin disease

cards.text: Then the priest sacrifices the sin offering to make atonement for him from his uncleanness, and after that he slaughters the burnt offering.

cards.question: The priest offers the burnt offering with the grain offering on the ___ to make atonement for him, and he will be clean.

cards.text: But what if the person is poor and can't afford all those offerings? Friend, I was bought for a quarter at a bakery's closing sale, so I LIKE where this is going.

cards.question: Along with a smaller grain offering and a log of olive oil, the poor person still brings one male ___ as a guilt offering.
Along with the lamb, the poor person brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons. How does he choose which?
For the poor person, the priest skips putting the blood and oil on his right earlobe, thumb and big toe.

cards.text: On the eighth day the priest walks through the same steps: the wave offering, the blood and oil on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe, and the rest of the oil on his head. Then come the two birds, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and the priest makes atonement for him before the LORD.
Then the LORD speaks to Moses and Aaron the priest, and now it's about houses. It's for when they enter the land of Canaan, which He is giving them, and He puts mildew into a house there.

cards.question: When mildew shows up in a house in that land, what is the owner of the house to do?

answers.text: Move his family out for good

cards.text: He tells the priest, "Something like mildew has appeared in my house." That's the opposite of painting over a stain and hoping nobody notices.

cards.question: Before going in to examine the mildew, the priest orders the house to be ___.
Why does the house get cleared out before the priest goes in to examine the mildew?

answers.text: So nothing in it becomes unclean
So the priest has room to work
So the owner can count his goods

cards.text: Inside, the priest looks for green or red depressions that appear to be beneath the surface of the wall. If that's what he finds, he steps outside the doorway and closes the house up for seven days.

cards.question: On the seventh day the priest comes back, and the mildew has spread on the walls. What happens to the contaminated stones?

answers.text: Pulled out and thrown outside the city
Washed off and put back in place
Piled up beside the house for a week

cards.text: The inside gets scraped completely, and the plaster goes to an unclean place outside the city. New stones and fresh mortar go in, and that's not cleaning, friend, that's a RENOVATION.

cards.question: If the mildew comes back and spreads after the new stones and plaster, the priest has the house scraped and replastered one more time.

cards.text: It's a destructive mildew, so the house is torn down: stones, timbers, plaster, all of it, out to an unclean place outside the city. Forget the RENOVATION, friend, this house is GONE.

cards.question: Anyone who goes into the house during the days it's closed up is unclean until evening.
God adds that anyone who sleeps in the house or eats in it must wash his ___.

cards.text: But if the priest inspects after the replastering and the mildew hasn't spread, he pronounces the house clean, because the mildew is gone. Best inspection report EVER.

To purify the house, the priest takes two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop, and slaughters one bird over fresh water in a clay pot. He dips the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the yarn in the blood and the fresh water, and he sprinkles the house seven times.
The live bird is released into the open fields outside the city. In this way he makes atonement for the house, and it will be clean.

cards.question: When God wraps up this law, He says it covers mildew in clothing too, not just mildew in a house.
This law covers skin diseases, scaly outbreaks, mildew, and any swelling, rash or spot. What is it all for?

answers.text: To tell when something is clean or unclean
To decide who can serve as a priest
To set the days for the yearly feasts

cards.text: And that's where we'll set it down for now, friend. Keep that oven warm, because this teaching on clean and unclean isn't finished yet.
